Specimen Type: Tissue biopsy, left breast

Clinical History: Palpable lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left
breast. Mammogram and ultrasound findings are suspicious for
malignancy.

Gross Description:

The specimen is received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name and medical record number, and
designated "left breast core biopsy." It consists of three tan-white, cylindrical tissue fragments,
ranging in length from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm and in diameter from 0.2 cm to 0.3 cm. The entire specimen is
submitted in one cassette.

Microscopic Description:

Histologic sections reveal cores of breast tissue with an infiltrative neoplasm. The tumor cells are
arranged in irregular nests and single files, infiltrating the fibrous stroma. The neoplastic cells are
pleomorphic with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Mitotic figures are
frequently identified. There is associated ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), solid type, with high-grade
nuclear features. No evidence of lymphovascular invasion is identified in the submitted material.
Diagnosis:

Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Grade 3 of 3.

Comments:

The histomorphologic features are those of a high-grade invasive ductal carcinoma. Correlation with
imaging findings and clinical presentation is recommended. Further evaluation for hormone receptor
status and HER2/neu expression is pending and will be reported in an addendum.

(a) Normal Colon

You have undergone a colonoscopy, a diagnostic procedure in
which a flexible, lighted tube was used to examine the lining of
your large intestine (colon). The sedation you received for the
procedure will continue to affect your judgment and coordination
for the rest of the day. For your safety, it is essential that you
carefully follow these instructions.

Immediate Post-Procedure Care

Transportation: You must be discharged into the care of a
responsible adult who will drive you home. You are not permitted
to drive, take a taxi or rideshare alone, or use public
transportation by yourself.

Rest and Supervision: A responsible adult must stay with you for
the remainder of the day and night. It is important to rest at home (b) Colon
for the rest of today.
Dietary Guidelines

Begin by drinking clear liquids (such as water, apple juice, ginger
ale, or broth) once you are home.

If you tolerate clear liquids well, you may advance to a light meal
a few hours later. Good choices include soup, toast, crackers, or
yogurt.

Impressions:

Normal Colonoscopy: The entire colon, from the cecum to the rectum, was visualized and appeared
normal. There were no polyps, masses, diverticula, or evidence of inflammation.

Activity: You may feel tired and bloated for the rest of the day. It is important to rest. Do not drive,
operate machinery, or make any important decisions for at least 24 hours. You must have a
responsible adult stay with you for the remainder of the day. You may resume normal activities
tomorrow.

Diet: You may resume your normal diet as tolerated. Start with clear liquids and light foods (e.g., soup,
gelatin, crackers) and advance to a regular diet if you are not experiencing nausea or significant
bloating. Avoid heavy, greasy, or spicy foods for the first 24 hours.

Follow-up: Based on the normal findings of your colonoscopy, your next routine screening
colonoscopy is recommended in 10 years. We will send a reminder to you at that time. If you
experience any severe abdominal pain, persistent nausea or vomiting, fever, or significant rectal
bleeding, please contact our office immediately or go to the nearest emergency room.

Procedure: MRI of the right knee without contrast.
Clinical Indication: Mechanical knee pain and locking sensation following a sports injury.

flipped fragment in the intercondylar notch. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Ligaments: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) shows high-grade sprain with fiber discontinuity,
consistent with a full-thickness tear. The posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), medial collateral ligament
(MCL), and lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex are intact.

Articular Cartilage and Bone: There is mild chondromalacia of the patellofemoral compartment. A
moderate-sized joint effusion is present. The visualized osseous structures show no evidence of acute
fracture, but there is bone marrow edema in the lateral femoral condyle and posterior tibial plateau,
suggestive of a pivot-shift contusion pattern.

Impression: Full-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). Complex, displaced tear of the
medial meniscus with a large fragment. Moderate joint effusion. Bone contusions consistent with a
pivot-shift injury.
